summary: Thomas Henry Huxley studied at Great Ealing School, University College London, Charing Cross Hospital and its Medical School (~1842-1845), and Imperial College School of Medicine. He held a post at Imperial College London from ~1854 to 1885.

Thomas Henry Thornton was an Indology and history scholar who studied at Merchant Taylors' School and St John's College, Oxford (~1850-1855). He was a Fellow at St John's (1855) and Calcutta (1875), and Vice-President of Punjab University (1879).

Thomas Holbein Hendley worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at St Bartholomew's Hospital (~1865-1869) and joined the Indian Medical Service in 1869, later serving as a Fellow at the University of Calcutta (1898-1903).

Thomas Howley was an Indology and linguistics scholar educated at Bishop Cowie's Grammar School. He served as Head-Master of the Anglo-Vernacular School, Professor at King's College London (1861), and taught Telugu at the University of Oxford (1878-1885).

Linguist Thomas Hudson-Williams studied at Ysgol Friars, University of London, Bangor University (~1890-1894), and Greifswald (~1894-1896) under Heinrich Zimmer. At Bangor, he served as Assistant Lecturer (1896, 1900) and Professor of Greek (1904-1940).

Thomas James Mazanec, a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies, earned degrees from Calvin University, CU Boulder, and Princeton University (Ph.D. 2017). He joined UC Santa Barbara, serving as Assistant Professor (2017-2023) and Associate Professor (attested 2026).

Thomas Jülch, a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies, studied at Frankfurt, Hull, Heidelberg, and Munich (PhD ~2005-2011). He held a postdoctoral research position at Ghent University from 2013 to 2019.
Thomas Kintaert is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who has held academic posts at the University of Vienna, attested there in 2009 and serving as a Lecturer (attested 2022-2026).
Thomas Lumisden Strange was an Indology scholar who was educated at Westminster School and the East India Company College from 1824 to 1826.
Thomas M. Hunter is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as Dean at the University of Virginia and was affiliated with the University of British Columbia (attested 2011).
Thomas Manning was a scholar in Tibetology and Sinology who studied as a Scholar at Gonville and Caius College (~1790-1795) and also studied at Westminster Hospital.

Thomas Maurice, an Indology and history scholar, studied at the University of Oxford (St John's College ~1774-1775, University College ~1775-1778; B.A. 1778, M.A. 1808). He was Assistant-Keeper of Manuscripts at the British Museum (1798-1824).

Thomas Nathan Patton, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, completed his PhD at Cornell University, where he studied under Anne M. Blackburn. He held a post at the City University of Hong Kong (attested 2018).

Thomas Oberlies, a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and religious studies, studied under Albrecht Wezler and Paul Thieme. He taught at Zurich (1990) and held posts at Tübingen, Freiburg, and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Thomas Oldham studied at Trinity College Dublin (B.A. ~1832-1836) and the University of Edinburgh. He served as Director of the Geological Survey of Ireland (1846) and Superintendent of the Geological Survey of India (1851-1876).

Thomas Procter was an Indology scholar who earned his B.A. from Jesus College, Oxford (1818-1824). He subsequently served as a Fellow at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1824-1826) and as an Examiner at Fort William College in 1828.

Thomas R. Trautmann is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He held posts at the University of Michigan, serving as co-director (attested 1980) and faculty member (attested 1991).
Thomas Robert Malthus studied at Warrington Academy from ~1782 to 1784 before completing his education at the University of Cambridge, attending Jesus College (~1784-1788).
Linguist Thomas Robinson studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (1808-1816; B.A., M.A., D.D.). He served at the University of Cambridge as the Lord Almoner’s Professor of Arabic from 1837 to 1854.

Thomas Roebuck, an Indology and linguistics scholar educated at the Royal High School, was assistant-secretary and examiner at the College of Fort St. George (1811) and examiner in Asian languages at Fort William College (~1811-1819).
